raw_case_text:
This is a 30-year old individual with CF having a Phe508del/Y1092X genotype, diffuse bronchiectasis colonized by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. In 2017, following an infectious exacerbation, the patient experienced an important pulmonary function decline (nadir FEV1 at 0.63 L, 23% of the predicted value) and had severe malnutrition (BMI 16 kg/m2). At that time, the transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) showed signs of pulmonary hypertension (dilated right ventricle and an estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure of 50 mmHg) and a patent foramen ovale. These results motivated a discussion for lung transplantation, an option the patient declined. Over the following years, FEV1 remained stable at 0.8 L (30% of predicted), but the patient's condition was precarious especially during infectious exacerbations. On February 2019, she presented with her lowest recorded value of FEV1 at 0.57L (21% of predicted), before receiving antibiotic treatment for an infectious exacerbation. In August 2020, ETI was initiated through the compassionate access program before its official approval in Switzerland on February 1, 2021. Following ETI initiation, the patient experienced a marked improvement of her general status and respiratory symptoms. The FEV1 increased up to 1.09L (40% of predicted) one month after starting ETI, nutritional status improved (BMI 18.2 kg/m2) and, since ETI start, the patient did not present any exacerbations requiring systemic antibiotics.
An unplanned pregnancy occurred in December 2021, around 4 months after ETI initiation, this being the first pregnancy for this patient. After a detailed genetic workup of the couple and following an extensive discussion about the risks of maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality in this setting, the patient decided to continue with the pregnancy. Despite the current scarcity of reproductive safety data, we pursued ETI considering the risk for maternal deterioration upon treatment cessation.
Close obstetric follow up confirmed normal fetal anatomy, growth and development over the course of pregnancy. Before the 31st week, the maternal pFEV1 remained between 35 and 40%, relatively stable compared to the values obtained immediately before the pregnancy (Fig. 1). Up to this time, the patient had not developed resting or nocturnal hypoxemia but the 6-min walking test showed exertional desaturation. In contrast to the TTE performed in summer 2017, the TTE carried out on the 13th and on the 31st week of gestation did not show a patent foramen ovale nor signs of pulmonary hypertension. There was no argument for allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) at any time-point, the patient did not develop gestational diabetes and an iron deficiency with mild anemia was substituted intravenously (IV) at the 31st and the 32nd week of pregnancy.
The course was uncomplicated until the 31st week when the patient presented symptoms of threatened preterm labour. She was hospitalized at the obstetric ward and received atosiban, followed by nifedipine for tocolysis and betamethasone for fetal lung maturation with a favorable evolution. At the same time, she contracted a rhinovirus infection causing a productive cough and bronchial congestion. A new oximetry showed nocturnal desaturation necessitating oxygen supplementation during sleep. The frequency of respiratory physiotherapy sessions was increased and inhaled formoterol/budesonide was also started. The patient refused concomitant antibiotic therapy and returned home after one week of hospital stay.
On the 33rd week of gestation, she developed symptomatic polyhydramnios treated with amniocentesis and drainage of 2700 ml of amniotic fluid. After a surveillance period of 12 hours post drainage, the patient was able to return home.
On the 36th week of pregnancy, she developed a spontaneous rupture of the membranes and gave birth to a healthy infant of 2.7 kg through vaginal delivery. To date, 12 months after delivery, the infant growth and development are uncomplicated. After childbirth, the nocturnal hypoxemia of the mother corrected rapidly and oxygen therapy was stopped. Four months after delivery, the FEV1 increased to 1.07L, 40% of the predicted value, at a similar level as before pregnancy (Fig. 1). The patient has also regained her baseline functional status.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old woman with severe cystic fibrosis (Phe508del/Y1092X) who stabilized on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) presented with an unplanned first pregnancy complicated in the third trimester by threatened preterm labor, rhinovirus bronchitis, nocturnal hypoxemia, and symptomatic polyhydramnios.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: With severe baseline cystic fibrosis lung disease (nadir FEV1 21% predicted in February 2019, BMI 16 kg/m2, and pulmonary hypertension), the patient started compassionate-use ETI in August 2020, improving her FEV1 to 1.09 L (40% predicted) and BMI to 18.2 kg/m2 without further antibiotic exacerbations. Four months after starting ETI (December 2021), she conceived an unplanned pregnancy and elected to continue both the pregnancy and ETI. Her FEV1 remained stable (35%-40% predicted) until 31 weeks' gestation, when she developed threatened preterm labor and a rhinovirus infection with productive cough and nocturnal hypoxemia, followed at 33 weeks by symptomatic polyhydramnios and at 36 weeks by spontaneous rupture of membranes.
subjective.past_medical_history: Cystic fibrosis (compound heterozygous Phe508del/Y1092X genotype) complicated by diffuse bronchiectasis chronically colonized by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, prior severe malnutrition (BMI 16 kg/m2), and prior pulmonary hypertension (PASP 50 mmHg) and patent foramen ovale in 2017 (both resolved on ETI).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive at 31 weeks' gestation for uterine contractions, rhinovirus-associated productive cough, bronchial congestion, and nocturnal oxygen desaturation, and at 33 weeks for abdominal distension from polyhydramnios.

objective.physical_examination: Pre-pregnancy BMI improved on ETI from 16 to 18.2 kg/m2. At 31 weeks' gestation, nocturnal oximetry showed sleep desaturation requiring nocturnal supplemental oxygen.
objective.routine_investigations: Spirometry showed pFEV1 maintained at 35%-40% throughout pregnancy and 1.07 L (40% predicted) at 4 months postpartum. Transthoracic echocardiograms at 13 and 31 weeks' gestation showed complete resolution of prior pulmonary hypertension and patent foramen ovale. Evaluations throughout pregnancy showed no evidence of allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) or gestational diabetes; mild iron-deficiency anemia at weeks 31-32 was treated with IV iron. Nasopharyngeal swab at week 31 was positive for rhinovirus.
objective.advanced_workup: Obstetric ultrasounds confirmed normal fetal anatomy and growth, and identified symptomatic polyhydramnios at 33 weeks' gestation requiring therapeutic amniocentesis (drainage of 2,700 mL of amniotic fluid).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Successful continuation of elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) therapy throughout pregnancy in a woman with severe cystic fibrosis (Phe508del/Y1092X), without allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) or gestational diabetes, complicated at 31 weeks by threatened preterm labor (treated with atosiban, nifedipine, and fetal maturation betamethasone) and rhinovirus bronchitis with nocturnal hypoxemia (treated with nocturnal oxygen, intensified chest physiotherapy, and inhaled budesonide/formoterol), and at 33 weeks by polyhydramnios (treated with 2,700 mL amnioreduction). She delivered a healthy 2.7-kg infant vaginally at 36 weeks' gestation, weaned off nocturnal oxygen immediately postpartum, and maintained her baseline FEV1 (1.07 L, 40% predicted) and infant health at 12 months postpartum.
